name_reason: Domain-correct name fd2_<domain=cutscene>_<descriptor=event_trigger>; no Ghidra address residue. The function is the numbered entry point that fires/plays a per-chapter cutscene walk-animation event selected by event_id, so 'cutscene' + 'event' + 'trigger' accurately reflects its role. 'trigger' (vs 'play') is a slightly loose but defensible descriptor for a synchronous event-firing entry point, and the name is already consistently used across 51 call sites + KB. Plate explicitly disclaims any audio meaning. Not worth churning 51 call sites/protos.h for a stylistic 'trigger'->'play' change.
purpose: Interpret a per-chapter cutscene byte-script (selected by event_id) and synchronously play out the encoded runtime-char walk-animation sequences, compositing/blitting frames and waiting BIOS ticks as it runs.
logic_summary: Looks up the script pointer via fd2_get_cutscene_event_script(event_id) into the 106-entry pointer table at 0x627D8. Script stream: [n_groups], then per group [walk_count_or_flags][step_count] followed by step_count interleaved (char_idx, dir) pairs (dir 0=south/+y, 1=west/-x, 2=north/-y, 3=east/+x). For each group, three modes selected by bit7 of walk_count_or_flags: (a) bit7==0 normal walk -> repeat low7 times: 6-frame animation setting each stepping char's sprite_state[1]=dir and sprite_state[2]=frame, composite frame each step (advancing the palette fade-in tween if cutscene_event_state in 1..0x3F), wait 1 tick + clear kbd; after the 6 frames commit pos_x/pos_y per dir and reset sprite_state[2]=0. (b) bit7==1 && low7==0 sprite-refresh blit pass -> recomposite the battle tile map into the work buffer (state buffer + 0x8088), paint each non-dead party member (temporarily offsetting the buffer pointer by -0x1560 for any char that is currently stepping, applying its dir), paint shadow overlay, blit the work rect to mode-13h framebuffer, wait + composite. (c) bit7==1 && low7!=0 facing-only/camera hold -> set facing for stepping chars then composite low7 frames without moving. Final composite_battle_frame(1) commits a clean frame.
